text: Mean Squared Error (MSE) is a standard loss function in supervised regression tasks. The mathematical formula is defined as: MSE = (1/n) * sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2, where y_i represents the ground truth value, \hat{y}_i represents the model prediction, and n is the total count of observations.

Embedding model dimension scaling directly dictates compute memory footprints and vector search latency. A 384-dimension vector (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2) consumes only 1.5 KB per vector and delivers high throughput (>130 chunks/s on CPU) with sub-millisecond query latency. In contrast, 1024-dimension models require over 4.1 KB per vector and exhibit higher query latency, making 384d ideal for edge computing and memory-constrained deployments.

Hierarchical chunking creates multi-level semantic trees: small child chunks (150-300 tokens) are indexed as dense vectors in ChromaDB or FAISS for high-precision similarity matching, while larger parent chunks preserve broader narrative context to avoid context fragmentation and prevent LLM hallucinations during generation.

ChromaDB provides persistent SQLite-backed relational metadata storage coupled with HNSW vector graph segments (hnswlib). It allows filtered metadata retrieval (where={'source': 'doc.pdf'}) with a modest ~2ms query overhead, while FAISS provides in-memory bare-metal C++ vector indexing with 0.2ms sub-millisecond search latencies.
